content.text:
I would keep **purple for MPs and teal for funders, and make general actions neutral**. Off-white primary buttons, neutral secondary controls, and a clear light focus ring would separate “what this is” from “what I can do” without adding another prominent colour.

| Option | Benefit | Tradeoff |
|---|---|---|
| **Neutral actions, existing entity colours** | Clearest separation; preserves the established MP/funder distinction | Actions need strong contrast, shape, and hover states |
| Third colour for actions | Strong action recognition while preserving both entity colours | Adds visual competition; amber overlaps warning semantics, while blue may suggest a political affiliation |
| Keep purple actions; change MP colour | Preserves the current action treatment | Requires relearning MP identity and revising the documented colour policy |
| Keep the palette; reduce purple on actions | Smallest visual change | Softens the ambiguity without removing it |

The underlying coupling is broader than button colour. [`tokens.css`](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/lib/ui/tokens.css:7) makes the general `--accent` default to the MP colour. [`actions.css`](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/lib/ui/actions.css:23) uses that same accent for actions and focus; [`patterns.css`](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/lib/ui/patterns.css:14) also uses it for search focus, caret, entity indicators, and badges. Search results distinguish funders by overriding that inherited accent in [`SearchPage.svelte`](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/SearchPage.svelte:334).

Whichever option you choose, separate **interaction colour from entity colour** first. Simply changing `--accent` would also recolour entity meaning. The subtle button and search glow contain literal purple values, so those would need attention too. The politically neutral appearance of off-white actions is a design judgment, not something verified with users.
